findings:
🔵 [retry-gate-truncated-any-error] CUT/FOLLOW-UP the non-success branch of isComplianceFlake keys on result.status === 'truncated' alone and does not also require result.error === 'frame_missing'; the spec names the retry class as truncated/frame_missing, and any other truncated error variant (if dispatch-author ever emits one) would also get the single bounded retry. Excluded because it is still "provider answered, not OK", it stays capped at two calls, and the envelope remains attributable; tighten to the error field only if dispatch-author gains a second truncated error code.
🔵 [worst-case-wall-time] CUT/FOLLOW-UP a slow compliance flake (long reply, then refusal) followed by a second long attempt can approach 2×200s inside the adapter since the per-attempt timeout is unchanged and timeouts themselves never retry. Excluded because typical flake replies are two tokens, spend is bounded to one extra call, and the spec asks for exactly one retry rather than a total-deadline budget.
🔵 [scratch-cwd-reused-across-attempts] CUT/FOLLOW-UP both attempts run from the same private scratch cwd, which is only removed in finally; any file dispatch-author leaves in cwd on attempt one is visible to attempt two. Excluded because the probe is declared repo-independent/read-only and no state-dependent behaviour is shown; a per-attempt subdirectory would be a hardening step, not a correctness fix.
